articles.originalTitle: Derrick Adams, Randy Polumbo, Wills Glasspiegel & More Artists Project Newly-Commissioned Works Onto Historic Hangars in Brooklyn - hyperallergic.com
articles.title: Major Public Art Festival to Transform Historic Brooklyn Airplane Hangars
articles.excerpt: Floyd Bennett Field, New York City's first airport, prepares for an annual public arts festival featuring large-scale projection-mapping projects and installations focusing on water themes and the Jamaica Bay landscape.
articles.content: The Floyd Bennett Field Public Arts Festival will return on Saturday, October 3, 2026, featuring 15 new works centered around water, nature, and innovation. New York City's first airport will host projects by renowned artists such as Derrick Adams, Randy Polumbo, Wills Glasspiegel, LaJuné McMillian, and Ryan Hartley Smith. The event utilizes projection-mapping onto the 8,640-square-foot facades of two monumental airplane hangars. The artworks explore the historic site's connection to the waterfront of Jamaica Bay and the Atlantic Ocean. Currently undergoing revitalization for future uses, the art-deco hangars will be brought to life for one night through light, movement, and digital storytelling. Drawing a diverse audience from across the region, the outdoor festival is free and open to all, offering visitors a combination of large-scale visual art, live music, and the natural surroundings of the park.

articles.originalTitle: About the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A Museum to Exhibit Istanbul's Artistic Heritage
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum is opening a new exhibition featuring artifacts from the Byzantine and Ottoman empires in November.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum in London will open the exhibition Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires on November 7, 2026. Spanning the years AD 330 to 1922, the presentation explores 1,600 years of artistic production across the Byzantine and Ottoman empires. Comprising four main sections, the exhibition showcases over 200 objects, including fine silks, textiles, ceramic tiles, mosaics, tableware, precious metalwork, jewelry, sculpture, architectural furnishings, manuscripts, and paintings. The Grand Beginnings section examines the city's refounding as the capital of a unified Roman Empire, while Heaven and Earth focuses on the integration of art and architecture with Christianity. Power and Reach highlights the visual spectacle and luxury materials of the Ottoman court. The final section, Life in the City, explores urban life, religious coexistence, and cosmopolitan traditions, concluding with the influence of both empires on nineteenth-century Europe.

articles.originalTitle: peter zumthor's expanded fondation beyeler opens to the public - Designboom
articles.title: Peter Zumthor’s Expansion of Fondation Beyeler Opens to the Public
articles.excerpt: Peter Zumthor’s expansion of the Fondation Beyeler in Riehen opens gradually, featuring three new buildings and nearly 10,000 square meters of parkland.
articles.content: Peter Zumthor’s expansion of the Fondation Beyeler in Riehen near Basel is opening to the public, with a gradual reveal starting 26 September 2026 ahead of a full opening in January 2027. The project introduces three new buildings—the Wyss Museum, Ammann Pavilion, and Erlen Torhaus—alongside an expanded park that opens nearly 10,000 square meters of formerly private land to visitors. The Wyss Museum adds approximately 1,500 square meters of exhibition space and is constructed using Jura limestone and a hand-built rammed-concrete facade. The Ammann Pavilion combines glass and oak to function as a public lounge during the day and a venue for cultural events seating up to 250 people in the evening. Historic structures such as the Orangerie and Ammann Atelier have also been restored for new educational and plant-focused uses. The surrounding landscape features artworks by creators including Alexander Calder, Jenny Holzer, Louise Bourgeois, and Pierre Huyghe.

articles.originalTitle: Google Unveils New Renderings of Chicago's Thompson Center Redesign, Marking Its Escape From Demolition - ArchDaily
articles.title: Chicago's Thompson Center Escapes Demolition with New Redesign Renderings
articles.excerpt: Chicago's postmodern James R. Thompson Center is being redeveloped as a space for work, culture, and community, escaping demolition through a collaboration with studio A+I.
articles.content: New redevelopment renderings have been released for the James R. Thompson Center in Chicago's Loop, designed by Helmut Jahn and completed in 1985. Commissioned by Governor James R. Thompson, the postmodern building features a multicolored glass atrium and a sloping corner entry. Facing criticism over maintenance costs and climate control issues, the structure was repeatedly threatened with demolition until preservationists campaigned for its protection. The building was sold to The Prime Group in 2022, and Google announced plans to purchase it following renovations. Renovations began in May 2024, involving the removal of portions of the original exterior and atrium. Developed in collaboration with Architecture Plus Information, now part of Perkins&Will, the redesign integrates food, retail, and seasonal event spaces into the 17-story atrium and plaza. The revamped public area will also house Vector, a 30-foot sculpture by artist Sanford Biggers, alongside a large-scale commissioned piece produced with the local nonprofit After School Matters.

articles.originalTitle: Standout Collectible Designs at Paris Design Week 2026 - WWD
articles.title: Standout Collectible Designs and Collections at Paris Design Week 2026
articles.excerpt: Paris Design Week marked its 16th edition with showrooms across Saint-Germain-des-Prés and beyond, featuring contemporary designs from 500 exhibitors.
articles.content: Paris Design Week took place from Sept. 10 to Sunday with the participation of 500 exhibitors, showcasing contemporary design and decor across the showrooms of Saint-Germain-des-Prés and beyond. Many creations were rooted in traditional techniques and natural forms. Modern Metier presented its second collection, Tropic of Capricorn, created with French designer Rudy Guénaire. Draga & Aurel showcased their new Crisalide side tables at Galerie BSL, combining colored glass and brass bases. Pinto teamed up with Nobilis to revive their collaboration with the Foundation collection. Yves Salomon Éditions unveiled Tactile Monuments, its first complete interior collection inspired by natural volumes and stones, pioneered by Tamara Taichman. Swedish design house Veermakers opened its first Paris showroom in Le Marais to highlight Scandinavian cabinetmaking traditions. Nordic Knots presented Dancing Flower and Matches, two hand-knotted wool rugs inspired by Swedish Grace. L’Objet partnered with Jessica McCormack on an exclusive home collection translating fine-jewelry craftsmanship into tabletop objects. Garnier & Linker unveiled Aurora, its first outdoor lighting collection. Franck Genser presented Piscine VI, while Hervet Manufacturier displayed its woodworking collections drawing on family heritage and cinema aesthetics.

articles.title: Theme and Artists Announced for the Inaugural Bienal de Yucatán
articles.excerpt: The inaugural Bienal de Yucatán, led by Abraham Cruzvillegas, will be titled VOCAL. The exhibition will take place from 26 November 2026 to 28 February 2027 across 16 venues in Mérida and Maní.
articles.content: The theme and participating artists for the inaugural Bienal de Yucatán have been announced. Led by Abraham Cruzvillegas, the exhibition is titled VOCAL and will run from 26 November 2026 to 28 February 2027 across 16 venues in Mérida and Maní. According to a statement by Cruzvillegas, the international exhibition will focus primarily on tongue, languages, idioms, the written, the spoken, and what needs to be said. The participating works and individuals will form an inclusion and diversity-focused event where languages and idioms engage in dialogue and contradict one another. A total of 76 artists are set to participate in the exhibition, including Alias, Abraham González Pacheco, Adolfo Bernal, Ahlam Shibli, Ana Hernández, André Cadere, Andy Medina, Antonio Caro, Augusto de Campos, Bárbara Sánchez Kane, Cachorra, Cecilia Vicuña, Chantal Peñalosa Fong, Citlalli Rodríguez, Coqueta, Dalila Hassanein, David Lamelas, Édgar Calel, Eun Sol Lee, Fabiola Torres-Alzaga, Federico Cuatlacuatl, Fernando García Correa, Gabriela Aguilar, Giuliana Aguirre, Jazael Olguín Zapata, Jean-Luc Moulène, Jerôme Bel, Jimmie Durham, Jonathas de Andrade, Jorge Pardo, José Ángel Santiago, José Chi, Karen Kantún, Julian Abraham Togar, Lawrence Weiner, Lenora de Barros, Luis Carlos Hurtado, Marcela Calderón Bony, Marco Castillo, Mariela Scafati, Marilita Quintana, Mario García Torres, Mauro Pech, Max Castañón, Mayra Silva, Melissa, Melquiades Herrera, Milana Gabriel, Miguel Fernández de Castro, Minerva Cuevas, Mitchell Urioste, Mónica Mayer, Mónica Mitre, Naomi Rincón Gallardo, Nicole, Óscar Murillo, Paloma Contreras Lomas, Proyectos Espectra, Rayyane Tabet, Rirkrit Tiravanija, Robert Filliou, Salomé Marejada, Salvador Xharicata, Sandra Gamarra, Sarah Konté, Susana Solís, Tania Pérez Córdova, Teresa Margolles, Tilsa Otta, Ulises Carrión, Valeria Sánchez, Verónica Gerber, Wael Shawky, Ximena Carrillo, Yael de Gorostegui, and Yoko Ono.

articles.originalTitle: "Modernity and Opulence: Women of the Wiener Werkstätte" at the Jewish Museum - hyperallergic.com
articles.title: Jewish Museum Exhibition Highlights Women Artists of the Wiener Werkstätte
articles.excerpt: The Jewish Museum in New York, in cooperation with the MAK Museum of Applied Arts in Vienna, presents an extensive exhibition examining the contributions of women designers and artists to modernist design within the Wiener Werkstätte.
articles.content: Modernity and Opulence: Women of the Wiener Werkstätte is on view at the Jewish Museum in New York from July 17 through November 15, 2026. Presented in cooperation with the MAK Museum of Applied Arts in Vienna, the exhibition highlights the central role of women, focusing particularly on Jewish women who worked as designers, artists, and patrons within the workshop. Active from 1903 to 1932, the Wiener Werkstätte was founded by architect Josef Hoffmann, artist Koloman Moser, and industrialist Fritz Waerndorfer. The exhibition features more than 200 objects across media such as fashion, ceramics, graphic design, decorative arts, and painting by approximately 30 women artists. Special emphasis is placed on Vally Wieselthier's ceramics and Felice Rix-Ueno's textile designs. The presentation also explores the workshop's international reach through the 1925 Paris International Exhibition of Modern Decorative and Industrial Arts and highlights Werkstätte ceramics featured in Hollywood films including The Kiss starring Greta Garbo.

articles.originalTitle: Paul Cezanne’s influence on generations of artists laid bare in Parisian exhibition - theartnewspaper.com
articles.title: Grand Palais Exhibition Explores Paul Cezanne and Intergenerational Influence
articles.excerpt: The Grand Palais in Paris is hosting a landmark exhibition examining Paul Cezanne's impact on generations of artists, from Picasso to Doig. Organized in partnership with major institutions, the show runs through 17 January 2027.
articles.content: The Grand Palais in Paris has opened a major exhibition dedicated to Paul Cezanne, organized through a partnership between the Centre Pompidou, the Musée d'Orsay, and the Musée de l'Orangerie. Prompted by the Pompidou's five-year closure for renovations, the presentation explores the French master's impact on contemporaries and subsequent generations of painters. Jean-Rémi Touzet, curator of paintings at the Musée d'Orsay, noted that the venue was chosen to make the most of its turn-of-the-century grandeur. The exhibition features 70 works by Cezanne alongside 75 pieces by artists ranging from Pablo Picasso and Henri Matisse to Piet Mondrian and Peter Doig. Curators have structured the layout both chronologically and thematically, focusing on core motifs such as landscapes, still lifes, and bathers. Among the notable loans is The Bather, coming from the Museum of Modern Art in New York. The exhibition runs from 23 September through 17 January 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Meet the Young Practices Shaping Architecture’s Next Chapter - Architizer
articles.title: Architizer Announces Winners of the 14th Annual A+Awards Best Young Firm
articles.excerpt: The winners of Architizer's 14th Annual A+Awards Best Young Firm category have been announced, highlighting emerging studios from diverse backgrounds that test the boundaries of architecture across climate, culture, and materials.
articles.content: The jury and public have selected the winners of Architizer's 14th Annual A+Awards, showcasing emerging practices that offer a glimpse into the future of the discipline. Jakarta-based RAD+ar won the jury prize for Best Young Firm through tropical architecture projects like Aruma Split Garden and Hidden Garden House. K-Thengono Design Studio received the popular choice award, utilizing vernacular methods and natural materials in Indonesia. Founded in Hong Kong and Shanghai, SKYnoa focuses on retail concepts blending Spanish, German, and Chinese perspectives. Toronto's PHAEDRUS Studio treats design as an open-ended dialogue across architecture and interiors. Shanghai-based EERI explores everyday essentials through multidisciplinary installations and architectural scales. Beijing Ger Architecture Technology specializes in prefabricated construction for rural revitalization and grassland communities in China. Chicago-based interior design studio Crespo & Br. centers its growing portfolio on hospitality projects. Finally, St. Louis practice AVV A integrates computational design, digital fabrication, and AI with traditional craft for cultural and public projects.

articles.originalTitle: Sansetsukon x Es Devlin: MILK - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Dance Collective Sansetsukon Performs New Live Work at V&A East Storehouse
articles.excerpt: Dance collective Sansetsukon is staging MILK, a new live performance responding to Es Devlin's installation The Everythingists, at the V&A East Storehouse.
articles.content: Dance collective Sansetsukon is presenting MILK, a new live performance responding to Es Devlin's installation The Everythingists through dance, sound, light, and shadow. Staged as a free special event on 3 October 2026 at the V&A East Storehouse, the performance creates a dialogue between the dancers, the installation, and the surrounding gallery space. The work draws inspiration from Rayonism and the concept of new art challenging old art, while also exploring ideas of humans empowered by machines and machines empowered by individuals. Set to an audio soundscape created by reworking material from The Everythingists, the 25 to 30-minute performance takes place across three sessions. The production features dancers including Joshua Shanny-Wynter, Deavion Brown, and Robbie Ordoña, alongside a creative team comprising composer Serian Griffiths and lighting designer Oliver Pritchard.

articles.originalTitle: The Big Review: Lucas Museum of Narrative Art ★★★½ - theartnewspaper.com
articles.title: The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art Opens in Los Angeles
articles.excerpt: Founded by filmmaker George Lucas in Los Angeles, the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art has opened its doors with a striking architectural design and a diverse collection spanning illustrations, comic books, and Star Wars artefacts.
articles.content: Founded by filmmaker George Lucas, the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art has opened in Exposition Park in Los Angeles. Designed by Ma Yansong of Mad Architects, the parabolic building features sweeping lines reminiscent of spacecraft. The museum's holdings draw heavily from illustration, comic books, manga, and film storyboards. Visitors entering the lobby are greeted by a life-size Naboo N-1 Starfighter, alongside gallery displays featuring original Star Wars artefacts such as Darth Vader's armour. The collection also includes works by artists and illustrators like Norman Rockwell, N.C. Wyeth, and Frank Frazetta, as well as murals by street artists including Banksy and JR. While the architectural scope and landscape design by Mia Lehrer have drawn attention, critics have raised questions regarding the absence of contextual wall labels and the inclusion of extensive reproductions throughout the galleries.

articles.originalTitle: 200,000 young people and counting: Tate celebrates a new generation with landmark commission for young artists - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Collective Reaches Record 200,000 Members With Landmark Commission
articles.excerpt: The free membership scheme Tate Collective reaches 200,000 members, celebrating the milestone with a new open call for emerging artists.
articles.content: Tate Collective, the free membership scheme for 16 to 25-year-olds, has reached a record 200,000 members. To mark the milestone, Tate launched an open call inviting members to create a new artwork for display at Tate Modern. The selected artist will exhibit alongside figures such as Andy Warhol, Salvador Dalí, and Marina Abramović. The winning commission will be selected by a jury chaired by Rosalie Doubal, Senior Curator at Tate, and will go on display in March 2027 following a submission deadline of 19 October. Concurrently, Tate Modern Lates marks its 10th anniversary after drawing 870,000 attendees over the past decade. Celebrations culminate on 30 October with a special anniversary event featuring multidisciplinary artist Shygirl transforming the South Tank into Club Shy, alongside contributions from Warp Records and Lakwena. Tate Collective offers members £5 exhibition tickets and discounts across cafés, bars, and shops, supported by The Rothschild Foundation and Tate Patrons.

articles.originalTitle: prada galleria unfolds across eight floors of fashion, art, history and pastry in milan - Designboom
articles.title: Prada Expands Historic Milan Headquarters Into an Eight-Floor Multi-Use Complex
articles.excerpt: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II in Milan, where Fratelli Prada opened its first store in 1913, has been transformed into an eight-floor complex featuring retail, art, archives, and hospitality.
articles.content: Prada has expanded its historic presence inside Milan’s Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II into an eight-floor complex spanning retail, hospitality, art, and archives. Named Prada Galleria, the project occupies the site where Fratelli Prada first opened in 1913. Developed under Miuccia Prada's direction, the multi-level destination features an underground passage known as the Passaggio Segreto, which connects the women's and men's boutiques and hosts an exhibition on the company's early history. The complex integrates Marchesi 1824 for pastry, Pradasphere as a permanent archival exhibition, private salon spaces, and Appartamento featuring an exhibition curated by Andreas Gursky. The uppermost level accommodates Osservatorio Fondazione Prada, dedicated to contemporary visual experimentation. The eight floors function as an integrated ecosystem combining fashion, cultural heritage, dining, and art.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale College Architettura 2026/2027: the 12 selected projects - labiennale.org
articles.title: Twelve Projects Selected for Biennale College Architettura 2026-2027
articles.excerpt: Twelve projects have been selected for the third edition of Biennale College Architettura. The projects by practitioners under 30 will be developed during a workshop from 22 to 30 September 2026.
articles.content: Twelve projects have been selected for the 3rd edition of Biennale College Architettura 2026–2027. The emerging practitioners under 30 originate from China, Croatia, Italy, Mexico, Syria, Spain, Turkey, Tunisia, the USA, and Hungary. The initiative complements the 20th International Architecture Exhibition, titled Do Architecture and curated by Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu, serving as a research, experimentation, and production laboratory. The open call attracted over 80 emerging practitioners from 36 countries. The 12 selected projects are presented by Ahlem Balghouthi, Fabio Bari, Stav Bouzaglo, Antonino Caridi, Yiying Chen, Alejandro Ferrer Esplugues, Jin Gao, Nisa Gökgöz, Matej Orkić, Julia Polefko, Ahmad Salah, and Guillermo Sanchez Cardenas. The workshop will take place from 22 to 30 September 2026, coordinated by Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu alongside tutors. Following the workshop, up to four projects will be selected to receive a 25,000 euro grant for the realization of the final work, which will be presented out of competition during Biennale Architettura 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Art Basel Paris 2026 Press Dossier: a deep-dive into this year's highlights - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Paris 2026 Opens with 211 Galleries and Expanded Programming
articles.excerpt: Hosting 211 galleries from 41 countries, Art Basel Paris prepares to open its doors in October with an expanded public program and numerous debut participants around the Grand Palais.
articles.content: Art Basel Paris prepares for its upcoming edition featuring 211 galleries from 41 countries and regions. The lineup includes 183 galleries in the Galeries sector, 16 in Emergence, and 12 in Premise. The fair features an expanded public program concentrated around the Grand Palais, alongside a first-time presentation at the Parvis des Droits-de-l'Homme. This year welcomes 32 first-time participants alongside over 170 returning galleries, with 6 exhibitors graduating from Emergence and more than 30 galleries younger than 10 years. The preview is scheduled for October 20, and Oh La La! returns under the art direction of Philippine Leroy-Beaulieu. France-based galleries continue to play a central role, accompanied by strong representation from international institutions. Petrine and The Pill make their debuts in the Galeries sector after previously showing in Emergence. Works by artists with notable museum exposure across French institutions this year will also be featured in various gallery presentations throughout the fair.

articles.originalTitle: Dezeen Awards 2026 architecture shortlist announced - Dezeen
articles.title: Dezeen Awards 2026 Architecture Shortlist Announced
articles.excerpt: The Dezeen Awards 2026 architecture shortlist features 152 projects across 19 categories by studios from 36 countries. Winners will be announced in London on November 16.
articles.content: Dezeen has announced the architecture shortlist for this year's Dezeen Awards, featuring 152 projects by studios located across 36 different countries. The shortlisted projects are competing in 19 different architecture project categories. Notable entries include a country house with unstabilised rammed earth walls in the UK, a trio of guesthouses with glass walls and thatched roofs in Ukraine, and a mosque with a stone-clad steelwork roof in Qatar. The selection also features an office reimagining machiya housing with metal awnings in Japan and a university building modelled on stepped wells in India. The projects were scored by an architecture jury including Annabelle Selldorf, Daniel Libeskind, Ma Yansong, Amanda Levete, and Norman Foster. The winner of each project category will be announced live on November 16 at the Royal Opera House in London. All category winners will then compete for the title of architecture project of the year.

articles.originalTitle: ARTIST ROOMS: Robert Rauschenberg at Tate Modern, 21 September 2026 - December 2027 – Press Release - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Modern to Host Major Free Exhibition of Robert Rauschenberg Works
articles.excerpt: Tate Modern is launching a large-scale free exhibition featuring over 20 works by American artist Robert Rauschenberg spanning three decades, including new donations marking his centennial.
articles.content: Tate Modern is hosting a large-scale free exhibition of works by Robert Rauschenberg from 21 September 2026 to December 2027. Bringing together over 20 works spanning three decades, the presentation features paintings, prints, kinetic works, and a selection of the artist's renowned Glut sculptures, including three newly gifted by the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation to mark his centennial. Part of the ARTIST ROOMS collection jointly shared by Tate and the National Galleries of Scotland, the display foregrounds the relationship between the works and the artist's engagement with dance and performance. Rauschenberg moved freely between painting, collage, sculpture, and photography, challenging traditional distinctions and incorporating everyday materials into his practice. His Glut series, created from scrap metal scavenged from junkyards, was seen by the artist as a warning against capitalist throwaway culture. Curated by Gregor Muir, Andrew de Brún, and Julia Blaut, the exhibition also features performance costumes, set adaptations, kinetic clocks, and textile works. The display is open daily at Tate Modern with free admission.

articles.originalTitle: Glenn Brown in: Fail We May, Sail We Must | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Brown Collection in London Opens New Exhibition
articles.excerpt: Curated by Glenn Brown and Edgar Laguinia, the exhibition brings together works by more than twenty artists.
articles.content: The Brown Collection in London has announced its upcoming exhibition titled Fail We May, Sail We Must. Scheduled to run from September 25, 2026, to August 7, 2027, the presentation is curated by Glenn Brown and Brown Collection cofounder Edgar Laguinia. The selection features historic and contemporary paintings, sculptures, drawings, prints, and ceramics spanning six centuries by more than twenty artists. Incorporating spliced collages, double images, and elongated figures with elements of playfulness and humor, the exhibition aims to establish new connections between works not commonly seen together. Separately, the latest issue of Gagosian Quarterly highlights works, conversations, and projects by Brice Marden, Jordan Wolfson, Cady Noland, Tyler Mitchell, Adriana Varejão, and Jennifer Guidi. Among the features, Adriana Varejão discusses her working practice in preparation for representing Brazil at the 61st Biennale di Venezia.

articles.originalTitle: How Architectural Fabrics Are Expanding the Role of the Building Envelope - ArchDaily
articles.title: Architectural Fabrics and Composite Membranes Expand the Building Envelope
articles.excerpt: Architectural composite fabrics support shading, acoustic treatment, and climate control strategies by adding performance layers to the building envelope.
articles.content: Architectural composite fabrics complement conventional building materials rather than replacing them, adding performance layers to the building envelope. At Gardens by the Bay in Singapore, more than 400 retractable textile shades concealed within steel arches mitigate solar heat gain. Placed outside the glass, the membrane intercepts radiant heat far more effectively than interior shading. In the renovation of Montreal's Biodome, architects introduced a continuous white textile membrane instead of conventional walls to wrap around ecosystems. The Tenseo Comfort AW textile skin absorbs reverberation within the public atrium, improving acoustic performance. Similarly, the thermal and architectural renovation of the Montpellier National School of Architecture integrates environmental functions into the facade assembly to reduce energy consumption by 60 percent. Across these projects, architectural composite fabrics enable building envelopes to adapt to climate conditions, enrich spatial experiences, and support passive environmental strategies.

articles.originalTitle: Maison Michel Celebrates 90 Years of Hatmaking With New Exhibition at Chanel’s Le19M - WWD
articles.title: Maison Michel Celebrates 90 Years of Hatmaking With New Paris Exhibition
articles.excerpt: Renowned Parisian hatmaker Maison Michel is marking its 90th anniversary with an exhibition at Chanel's craftsmanship hub Le19M, showcasing ancient tools, wooden hat blocks, and the intricate production processes behind its iconic millinery.
articles.content: Parisian hatmaker Maison Michel is celebrating its 90th anniversary with an exhibition titled 'Metamorphoses — The Hats of Maison Michel' at La Galerie du 19M, Chanel's craftsmanship hub in northern Paris. Running until December 13, the exhibition is curated by artistic director Priscilla Royer and Palais Galliera fashion museum director Emilie Hammen. The display brings together raw linden wood blocks, archival wooden hat blocks, specially commissioned artworks by creators like Amaury Darras, and iconic runway headwear spanning decades. Visitors can explore the intricate production steps inside the Maison Michel workshop, from steaming and baking felt forms to sewing straw on 19th-century machines. The exhibition space also features a replica of an early 20th-century milliner's shop where weekly filmmaking workshops are hosted by Michel Gondry's L'Usine de Films Amateurs studio. The showcase highlights the evolution of headgear from a social signifier into a modern form of personal expression.

articles.originalTitle: 6 artists to watch at the Lyon Biennale 2026 - Art Basel
articles.title: 18th Lyon Biennale Opens with Works by 118 International Artists
articles.excerpt: Curated by Catherine Nichols, the 18th Lyon Biennale brings together 118 artists from around the world across historical venues in Lyon between September and December.
articles.content: Founded in 1991, the Lyon Biennale returns for its 18th edition, running from September through December across key venues in the city. Entrusted to Australian writer and art historian Catherine Nichols, currently at the Hamburger Bahnhof in Berlin, the ambitious program brings together 118 artists from around the globe. Titled To Pass from One Dream to Another and inspired by Lyon's traboules passageways, the exhibition draws on Robert Filliou's principles of poetic economy. Nichols has organized the presentation around three distinct layers: the existential at macLYON, the relational at the Musée des Tissus et des Arts décoratif, and the industrial at Les Grandes Locos. The edition features a strong presence from the Oceanian scene and showcases works by artists including Akwasi Bediako Afrane, Hana Miletić, Serwah Attafuah, Luke Willis Thompson, Angela Goh, and Minh Lan Tran, offering audiences an opportunity to discover practices rarely shown in France.
